content: The references provided are a list of studies and reports that focus on various aspects of HIV/AIDS treatment, adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART), and related interventions. 1. Paton NI et al. (2006): This study investigates the effects of malnutrition on survival rates and CD4 count responses in HIV-infected patients initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART). The findings highlight the critical role of nutritional status in influencing treatment outcomes. 2. van der Sande MA et al. (2004): The research identifies body mass index (BMI) at the time of HIV diagnosis as a significant and independent predictor of survival, emphasizing the importance of early nutritional assessment in HIV care. 3. WHO Multicentre Growth Reference Study Group: This report outlines the development and methodology of WHO child growth standards, which are essential for monitoring the growth and health of children globally, including those affected by HIV. 4. Mills EJ et al. (2006): A systematic review examines barriers and facilitators to adherence to highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) in both developed and developing nations, based on patient-reported data. 5. Martin S et al. (2007): This study explores factors associated with adherence to HAART among HIV-infected children and adolescents, focusing on patient, caregiver, and regimen characteristics. 6. Reddington C et al. (2000): The research evaluates medication adherence among children with HIV, identifying challenges and potential strategies to improve adherence rates. 7. Murphy DA et al. (2001): This study examines adherence to antiretroviral medication among HIV-infected adolescents in the REACH cohort in the USA, highlighting unique challenges faced by this population. 8. Dowshen N, D’Angelo L (2011): The authors discuss healthcare transition strategies for youth living with HIV/AIDS, emphasizing the need for tailored approaches to ensure continuity of care. 9. Duff P et al. (2010): This study identifies barriers to accessing HAART among HIV-positive women attending antenatal clinics in western Uganda, providing insights into gender-specific challenges in HIV care. 10. Nachega JB et al. (2012): A systematic review and meta-analysis assess adherence to ART during and after pregnancy across low-, middle-, and high-income countries, highlighting disparities and areas for improvement. 11. Nakimuli-Mpungu E et al. (2012): This review examines the impact of depression and alcohol use on ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing the need for integrated mental health and substance use interventions. 12. Gonzalez JS et al. (2011): A meta-analysis explores the relationship between depression and non-adherence to HIV/AIDS treatment, underscoring the importance of addressing mental health in HIV care. 13. Bottonari KA et al. (2012): The study identifies correlates of adherence to both antiretroviral and antidepressant medications among HIV-infected patients with depression. 14. Springer SA et al. (2012): This systematic review evaluates the impact of DSM-IV mental disorders on adherence to combination ART among adults living with HIV/AIDS. 15. Altice FL et al. (2011): A multisite study investigates HIV treatment outcomes among opioid-dependent patients receiving buprenorphine/naloxone treatment within HIV clinical care settings. 16. Roux P et al. (2008): The MANIF 2000 cohort study examines the effects of methadone or buprenorphine treatment and ongoing injection drug use on HAART adherence. 17. Malta M et al. (2010): A meta-analysis assesses adherence to ART among HIV-infected drug users, identifying factors that influence adherence in this population. 18. Rich JD et al. (2011): The authors advocate for increased HIV-related research in correctional populations, highlighting the unique challenges and opportunities in this setting. 19. Bärnighausen T et al. (2011): A systematic review evaluates interventions aimed at increasing ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, providing evidence-based recommendations for improving treatment outcomes. 20. Chung MH et al. (2011): A randomized controlled trial compares the effects of counseling and alarm devices on HAART adherence and virologic outcomes. 21. Rueda S et al. (2006): This Cochrane review examines the effectiveness of patient support and education interventions in promoting adherence to HAART for HIV/AIDS. 22. Altice FL et al. (2001): The study explores the role of trust in the acceptance of and adherence to ART, emphasizing the importance of patient-provider relationships. 23. Decroo T et al. (2011): The research evaluates the distribution of ART through self-forming patient groups in Mozambique, highlighting innovative approaches to improving access and adherence. 24. Lucas GM et al. (2006): The study demonstrates that directly administered ART in methadone clinics is associated with improved HIV treatment outcomes compared to concurrent comparison groups. 25. Cantrell RA et al. (2008): A pilot study investigates the impact of food supplementation on ART adherence among food-insecure adults in Zambia. 26. Muñoz M et al. (2010): This study evaluates community-based directly observed therapy for HAART in an urban resource-poor setting. 27. Haberer JE et al. (2010): The authors discuss challenges in using mobile phones to collect ART adherence data in resource-limited settings. 28. Sidney K et al. (2012): The study explores the use of mobile phone reminders to support ART adherence in South India, reporting positive patient responses. 29. Lester RT et al. (2010): A randomized trial in Kenya assesses the effects of mobile phone SMS on ART adherence, demonstrating significant improvements in treatment outcomes. 30. Ikeda JM et al. (2013): The study evaluates the impact of SMS messaging on treatment outcomes among HIV-positive Mayan populations in rural Guatemala. 31. Pop-Eleches C et al. (2011): A randomized controlled trial investigates the effectiveness of text message reminders in improving ART adherence in resource-limited settings. 32. Curioso W et al. (2012): This dissertation evaluates a computer-based system using cell phones for HIV-infected individuals in Peru. 33. Ammasari A et al. (2011): The study demonstrates that timed SMS improves adherence and virological outcomes in HIV-1-infected patients with suboptimal ART adherence. 34. da Costa TM et al. (2012): A randomized controlled trial assesses the effects of an SMS-based intervention on ART adherence among HIV-infected Brazilian women. 35. Mbuagbaw L et al. (2012): The CAMPS trial compares text messaging versus usual care for ART adherence in Cameroon. 36. Dowshen N et al. (2012): A pilot study evaluates personalized, interactive daily text message reminders to improve ART adherence among youth living with HIV/AIDS. 37. Uzma Q et al. (2011): The study examines the efficacy of interventions to improve ART adherence in HIV/AIDS cases at PIMS, Islamabad. 38. Wamalwa DC et al. (2009): A randomized clinical trial in Kenya finds that medication diaries do not improve outcomes with HAART in children. 39. Mugusi F et al. (2009): The Tanzanian experience highlights strategies to enhance ART adherence in resource-constrained settings. 40. Bisson GP et al. (2008): The study compares pharmacy refill adherence with CD4 count changes for monitoring HIV-infected adults on ART. 41. Ndubuka NO et al. (2011): A survey correlates pharmacy refill records and pill counts with immunological and virological indices to assess ART adherence. 42. McMahon J et al. (2011): A review of pharmacy adherence measures provides insights into their implications for ART treatment monitoring. 43. Minzi OM, Naazneen AS (2008): The study validates self-report and hospital pill count methods for determining ART adherence using unannounced home pill counts. 44. Kalichman SC et al. (2007): The research assesses ART adherence through unannounced pill counts conducted via telephone. 45. Zolopa A et al. (2009): A multicenter randomized trial finds that early ART reduces AIDS progression and death in individuals with acute opportunistic infections. 46. Blanc FX et al. (2011): The study compares earlier versus later initiation of ART in HIV-infected adults with tuberculosis. 47. Fox MP, Rosen S (2010): A systematic review examines patient retention in ART programs up to three years in sub-Saharan Africa. 48. Mugglin C et al. (2012): A systematic review and meta-analysis quantify losses along the continuum of care for people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa. 49. Brinkhof MW et al. (2009): The study evaluates mortality among patients lost to follow-up in ART programs in resource-limited settings. 50. Kranzler K et al. (2012): A systematic review addresses losses along the continuum of care for HIV-infected individuals in sub-Saharan Africa. 51. WHO, UNAIDS, UNICEF (2011): The progress report provides a global overview of the HIV/AIDS response. 52. Sprague C et al. (2011): A qualitative inquiry identifies health system weaknesses that constrain access to PMTCT and maternal HIV services in South Africa. 53. Bwirire LD et al. (2008): The study investigates reasons for loss to follow-up among mothers in a PMTCT program in rural Malawi. 54. Killam WP et al. (2010): A stepped-wedge evaluation examines the impact of integrating ART into antenatal care for HIV-infected pregnant women. 55. Ong’ech JO et al. (2012): The study compares maternal and child health clinic models with HIV comprehensive care clinic models for HIV-exposed infants. 56. Turan J et al. (2012): A cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluates the effects of integrating antenatal care and HIV services on PMTCT outcomes in Kenya. 57. Washington S et al. (2012): The study assesses the impact of integrating HIV care into antenatal clinics on mother-to-child HIV transmission and maternal outcomes in Kenya. 58. Vo BN et al. (2012): The research evaluates patient satisfaction with integrated HIV and antenatal care services in rural Kenya. 59. Tsague L et al. (2010): The study compares two service delivery models for PMTCT during the transition from single-dose nevirapine to multidrug ART regimens. 60. Winestone LE et al. (2012): A qualitative provider interview study examines the acceptability and feasibility of integrating HIV care services into antenatal clinics in rural Kenya. 61. Havlir DV et al. (2011): The study investigates the timing of ART initiation for HIV-1 infection and tuberculosis. 62. Blanc FX et al. (2011): The research compares earlier versus later ART initiation in HIV-infected adults with tuberculosis. 63. Suthar AB et al. (2012): A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the effect of cotrimoxazole on mortality in HIV-infected adults on ART. 64. Bento C et al. (2012): The study assesses the effectiveness of a home-based care program for patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV after hospital discharge.
